title: Four linked anti-COVID-measures rallies in Central Switzerland
location: Schwyz (Hauptplatz), with parallel live-screen venues in Altdorf (Lehnplatz), Stans (Dorfplatz), and Sarnen (Landenberg)
scope: Coordinated multi-site Central Switzerland action spanning Schwyz, Uri, Nidwalden and Obwalden; event-unit scope pending review
organizer: Aktionsbündnis Urkantone für eine vernünftige Corona-Politik
participants_original: Keystone-SDA reported over 1,000 across four permitted gatherings and police-sourced estimates of about 400 in Schwyz, about 200 in Sarnen, about 300 in Stans, and 220 in Altdorf. Blick observed about 250 at Schwyz shortly before 16:00 and nearly 400 shortly before 17:00; it attributed 1,300 across four sites to speakers.
threshold_50_evidence: Each reported site count independently exceeds 50: approximately 400 in Schwyz, 200 in Sarnen, 300 in Stans and 220 in Altdorf, based on cantonal-police estimates relayed by Keystone-SDA; BLICK independently describes hundreds at Schwyz. The unresolved issue is whether the four separately permitted but coordinated parallel venues form one MM event or multiple events.

start_date.summary: Contemporaneous report and organizer notice date the four linked rallies to Saturday 9 January 2021.

location.summary: The organizer lists Schwyz, Altdorf, Stans and Sarnen; reports describe Schwyz as the primary event and the other sites as parallel live-screen venues.

scope.summary: One organizer arranged simultaneous parallel assemblies with transmission from Schwyz. They were separately permitted and locally counted, so event-unit scope remains pending.

organizer.summary: Organizer page and Keystone-SDA identify the Aktionsbündnis Urkantone.

demands.summary: Reports explicitly describe the gatherings as opposition to COVID measures or stricter pandemic restrictions, i.e. state policy.

participants_original.summary: Keystone-SDA reports >1,000 combined and canton-police estimates by site; Blick reports changing Schwyz observations and attributes a four-site 1,300 estimate to speakers.

participants_min.summary: 1,000 is the lower end of the reported combined 'over 1,000' estimate; it is not an exact count.

participants_max.summary: 1,300 is the aggregate figure attributed by Blick to speakers, not an independently measured maximum.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: All four site estimates and independent Schwyz observations are well above 50; site-level accounts are retained without summing into a new exact total.

protester_violence.summary: Keystone-SDA says the gatherings were peaceful, Blick reports no incidents in Schwyz, and the Kapo NW-attributed Stans account says calm and without problems.

accommodation.summary: Four venues were permitted and police monitored conditions; no evidence shows negotiation or accommodation of the substantive demand to change COVID policy, so response is unknown.

arrests.summary: Four Schwyz participants were reported to the prosecutor for mask-rule violations; this does not establish arrest, so arrests remain unknown.

beatings.summary: No account establishes state beatings; silence is not coded as no.

crowd_dispersal.summary: Reports describe permitted gatherings and police monitoring, not a dispersal attempt; response remains unknown.

ignore.summary: No source documents explicit governmental avoidance or refusal to engage; response remains unknown.

killings.summary: No source describes state-caused killing; response remains unknown.

shootings.summary: No source describes police firearm use; response remains unknown.

end_date.summary: Schwyz and Stans reports give roughly two-hour site durations, while the organizer gives a planned schedule; completion of all four physical sites is not fully established, so overall end date is unknown.

start_precision.summary: Contemporaneous reports and organizer material give the calendar date as 9 January 2021.

end_precision.summary: Available site schedules and reports do not establish one physical endpoint for all four sites; precision remains unknown.

title.summary: The reports identify coordinated anti-COVID-measures gatherings at four Central Switzerland sites.

notes: The same organizer scheduled four parallel gatherings, with Schwyz as the live-transmitted main event and three separate local assemblies. The sites had separate permits and separate counts. Retain one coordinated multi-site candidate for coordinator unit review; do not automatically merge or split by city. The reported counts are source-scoped: Keystone-SDA's combined >1,000 and local police estimates, Blick's time-specific Schwyz observations, and a speaker-attributed 1,300 total. participants_min/max represent the low and high ends of published combined estimates, not statistical bounds or a new exact count. Four Schwyz citations to prosecutors are not coded as arrests.
open_questions: Should the four separately permitted simultaneous rallies linked by organizer and live transmission be one MM event or multiple local events under the unavailable additional Coding Procedure?
Can primary police-hosted releases for Sarnen and Altdorf be located? Nau reports police-sourced counts, but only third-party-republished local police material was read for Schwyz and Stans.
Did all four site gatherings end at the same time? Organizer schedule and two-hour site reports do not establish the final physical endpoint of the entire multi-site action.
The 1,300 all-site figure is attributed to speakers; no independent combined count is available.

title: Zurich walk against COVID-19 measures
location: Münsterhof, Münsterbrücke, Limmatquai and Niederdorf, Zurich
participants_original: The Stadtpolizei Zürich account says several hundred people gathered at Münsterhof; no more precise turnout is given.
threshold_50_evidence: The official city account's description 'several hundred people' clearly exceeds 50.

start_date.summary: The official release dates the walk to Saturday afternoon, 30 January 2021.

location.summary: The official release says several hundred gathered at Münsterhof, moved toward Münsterbrücke, then regrouped at Limmatquai/Niederdorf.

scope.summary: One Zurich city walk with a subsequent regrouping at another nearby location is described in the same police account.

demands.summary: The city describes the walk as being against COVID measures, a policy of the Swiss domestic state.

participants_original.summary: The city reports several hundred at Münsterhof without an exact count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The official description 'several hundred' is well above the 50-person threshold.

protester_violence.summary: The source does not make an explicit event-level claim about protester violence.

accommodation.summary: No negotiation or accommodation of the demand is reported; the record does not infer either response from silence.

arrests.summary: Four people were taken to a police station for further inquiries, but the source does not identify formal arrests; response remains unknown.

beatings.summary: The account does not report state beatings; response remains unknown.

crowd_dispersal.summary: Police blocked Münsterbrücke, made loudspeaker announcements, then later checked participants and ordered them away after groups reassembled. This supports an attempted crowd-dispersal response; it does not establish the full episode's final physical endpoint.

ignore.summary: No explicit refusal or avoidance of the demand is reported; response remains unknown.

killings.summary: The account does not report a state-caused killing; response remains unknown.

shootings.summary: The account does not report police firearm use; response remains unknown.

end_date.summary: The police operation ended shortly before 16:00, after participants left in groups, regrouped and were later ordered away. The account does not establish the final physical endpoint of the protest episode.

organizer.summary: The opened municipal-police account does not identify an organizer; no organizer is assigned.

participants_min.summary: The city account says 'several hundred' without a numerical lower bound that can be represented as a defensible participant minimum; left null.

participants_max.summary: The city account says 'several hundred' without a numerical upper bound; left null.

start_precision.summary: The municipal account dates the gathering to 30 January 2021.

end_precision.summary: The city reports when its operation ended, but not when the physical gathering ended; event end precision remains unknown.

title.summary: The municipal-police account describes a 30 January walk in Zurich against COVID measures.

notes: Official city account provides date, site, several-hundred turnout, public-policy target and a specific police dispersal attempt. The crowd's first departure was followed by regrouping, and the police-operation end is not necessarily the episode end; end_date remains unknown. Four people were taken to a police station for further inquiries and dozens were cited, neither of which alone proves formal arrests.
open_questions: The official account does not name an organizer.
No precise numeric attendance estimate or independent report was located yet.

Did all participants leave after police began checks and ordering them away? The official report ends with the police operation shortly before 16:00 but does not explicitly state complete final dissolution.
Were the four people taken for inquiry formally arrested? The source does not say.

title: Bundesplatz anti-COVID-restrictions protest in Bern
location: Bundesplatz in front of the Federal Palace and nearby Bern streets
scope: Local Bern demonstration with some participants continuing through the city after police orders
participants_original: About 100 people, according to the opened Keystone-ATS report.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened contemporaneous report estimates about 100 people at the public assembly, clearly above 50.

start_date.summary: The opened report gives publication time 23 January 2021, 16:19, and says the gathering occurred that afternoon.

location.summary: The report places about 100 people on the square before the Federal Palace in Bern.

scope.summary: One Bern gathering is described, with some participants followed and checked at other city locations after police intervention.

demands.summary: The report says participants protested government-imposed pandemic restrictions and called for an end to the measures.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The explicit 'about one hundred' estimate establishes a group above 50.

protester_violence.summary: The opened account describes the protest and police response but does not explicitly establish absence or presence of protester violence.

accommodation.summary: No meeting, negotiation or acceptance of demands is reported.

arrests.summary: Two same-agency Keystone-ATS versions say several participants who did not follow police directions were stopped and reported; neither specifies formal arrest status. The blocked BLICK search-result lead reports about 60 citations, which is not treated as arrest evidence; arrests remain unknown.

beatings.summary: No state beating is reported; response remains unknown.

crowd_dispersal.summary: The two opened Keystone-ATS versions say police interrupted the event, ordered participants to leave by loudspeaker, cordoned the square and checked those remaining; most left after the announcement. This is an explicit dispersal attempt.

ignore.summary: The police response is reported; no separate government avoidance/refusal to address the demand is documented.

killings.summary: No state-caused killing is reported; response remains unknown.

shootings.summary: No police firearm use is reported; response remains unknown.

end_date.summary: Most participants reportedly left after the loudspeaker announcement, while some were followed and checked at other city locations. The report does not establish final episode dissolution, so end_date is unknown.

organizer.summary: The Keystone-ATS report describes a call shared through social media but does not identify an organizer.

participants_min.summary: The agency report estimates 'about 100' without a defensible numerical lower bound; left null.

participants_max.summary: The agency report estimates 'about 100' without a defensible numerical upper bound; left null.

start_precision.summary: The report dates the assembly to 23 January 2021.

end_precision.summary: The report documents participants leaving and being checked but does not establish the gathering’s final physical endpoint; precision remains unknown.

title.summary: The Keystone-ATS report describes a 23 January Bern gathering against COVID restrictions.

notes: The opened SWI article is a Keystone-ATS report. A BLICK search result independently surfaces about 100 participants and roughly 60 police citations, but the exact BLICK page returned HTTP 403 and is not relied upon as body evidence. The Italian report says several participants who failed to follow police directions were stopped and reported; formal arrest status is unclear, so arrests remain unknown. Police orders and cordoning support crowd_dispersal=yes. The report says most left after the order, but some continued through the city under police observation; no final end date is inferred. A second opened reproduction in Corriere del Ticino (S076) is the same Keystone-ATS report as S070, not an independent confirmation.
open_questions: Who organized the Bern rally? The opened article only says a social-media call circulated.
Does the article's Italian 'fermate' mean formal arrests or police stops/custody? No number or exact arrest status is stated; citations are not coded as arrests.
Did the whole episode end after participants left the square, or did the walking groups remain part of the protest? No final physical endpoint is stated.

Is this one discrete event in a recurring weekend campaign, or part of a continuous episode? The source says similar weekend calls had occurred for some time, but no start date or continuity is established.

title: Anti-COVID-measures gathering at Bern's Bundesplatz
scope: One gathering on Bern's Bundesplatz; an inaccessible Blue News article search result mentions a small march in the old town, but that route is not coded from the snippet.
participants_original: Nau and a police-news republication attributed to Kantonspolizei Bern say several dozen people gathered. Nau says about 25 remained after police ordered them to leave; that is not the initial crowd size.
threshold_50_evidence: The occurrence of a public gathering and opposition to COVID measures are documented, but the two opened accounts describe the initial crowd only as several dozen. About 25 is the number who stayed after a police order, not a total attendance estimate. No read body establishes at least 50; eligibility remains pending_threshold.
